subject: Mars dust devil
title: Lightning on Mars Was Found by a Microphone, Not a Camera

scenes.text: Lightning on Mars was found by a microphone, not a camera.
NASA's Perseverance rover recorded fifty-five strange snaps over two Martian years.
At first, scientists blamed one of them on a grain of sand hitting the mic.
But the snaps came when dust devils and dust storms swept right over the rover.
Spinning dust builds up static, and Mars' thin air lets it jump as sparks only a few centimetres long.
So yes, Mars has lightning. It's about as strong as the shock from a doorknob.

description:
Lightning on Mars was finally confirmed, and it was heard, not seen.
NASA's Perseverance rover's SuperCam microphone picked up 55 electrical discharges over two Martian years, mostly when dust devils passed overhead or dust storm fronts rolled through. The arcs are only a few centimetres long, roughly as strong as a static shock from a doorknob, because Mars' thin air needs far less charge to spark.
Would you want to stand inside a Martian dust devil?
first_comment: Bonus: in 1971 the Soviet Mars 3 lander went silent about 20 seconds after touching down in a dust storm, and one researcher says an electrical discharge can't be ruled out. Would you risk landing in one?
